clue.text: Another bridge player without hearts? Start the contest!

parts.note: a second helping is another one

indicators.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts, so this phrase drops that letter from the player

parts.note: South is one of the four seats at a bridge table

explanation.surface: A card player asks for a replacement partner, then calls for the game to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hearts' takes H from SOUTH, leaving SOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry to boxers' helpers to leave the ring as a round begins.

clue.text: Opening in which drunkard swallows litre

indicators.note: a drunkard swallowing something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A gap through which a heavy drinker downs a litre of booze.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a narrow aperture, as in a coin slot.

clue.text: Youngster left in bed

indicators.note: the word in places the abbreviation within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, especially a child's

explanation.surface: A child abandoned in its bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, and by extension an inexperienced young player.

clue.text: Networking allowing one to assume a modicum of power?

definitions.text: Networking allowing one to assume a modicum of power?

parts.words: Networking allowing one to assume a modicum of power?
parts.note: reads like social networking for the ambitious, but describes the country's linked electricity supply that lets every home draw a little power

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests career networking and grabbing power; the real network is the British electricity transmission system.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's high-voltage cable system distributing electricity across the country.

clue.text: Fish turning up in sources of water

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fish turning up in sources of water' with no enumeration; no reading of these words gives the letters, so the clue looks cut short or misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Fish turning up in sources of water

clue.text: Absolute expert penning new speech

parts.note: utter means complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen encloses animals, so the expert surrounds the letter

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A complete expert writes a fresh address to deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing: ACE holds N to make ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something spoken aloud, a remark or speech.

clue.text: Member? Liberal's brought in Member

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so the abbreviation goes within the party's short form

parts.note: Lib is the short form of Liberal
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: An MP asks whether the Liberals have admitted a new parliamentarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two different jobs: the first is the definition, the second supplies M.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body.

clue.text: Undertaking to pass another vehicle here?

definitions.text: Undertaking to pass another vehicle here?

parts.words: Undertaking to pass another vehicle here?
parts.note: undertaking is overtaking on the wrong side, which a driver does from the lane nearest the kerb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaking' suggests a funeral business or a promise; on the road it means passing on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The lane nearest the verge on a motorway, used when passing a slower car on the wrong side.

clue.text: Poet capturing English judge along with one painter

indicators.note: the poet captures the other letters, holding them inside his name

parts.note: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet

explanation.surface: A poet seizes an English judge and another artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Burne-Jones was a Victorian Pre-Raphaelite artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Burne-Jones was a Victorian artist associated with the Pre-Raphaelites.

clue.text: Expunge opening of odd book, being able to read

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: literate describes someone who can read

explanation.surface: Wipe out the start of a strange volume, now that you can read it.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge is to erase or wipe out completely.

clue.text: One thinking to remove first drug addict

indicators.note: the first letter of the thinker is dropped from the front

parts.note: a muser is someone who muses or ponders

explanation.surface: A thoughtful person resolves to get rid of a drug habit first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove first' drops M from MUSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes illegal drugs habitually.

clue.text: Proscribing chess player's inclination?

parts.note: the dark-pieces side at chess leaning over would be the black side tilting, which sounds like a word for banning

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into the colour of one chess side plus a lean, as of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting names on a banned list is proscribing them.

clue.text: Stick with the beers in university locale

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so porters are beers
to lodge is to become stuck or fixed

explanation.surface: Stay put with the ales somewhere on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces, which run in reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The gatehouse at a college entrance where the custodian sits.

clue.text: Not like a book with vague characterisation?

definitions.text: Not like a book with vague characterisation?

parts.words: Not like a book with vague characterisation?
parts.note: read characterisation as the letters printed, and vague as small or hard to see: such a book is the opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Characters here are printed letters, not people in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Big type for readers with poor sight, the opposite of tiny faint characters.

clue.text: Disarrayed Tories daily losing heart of their collective nature

indicators.note: something disarrayed is in disorder, so these letters are jumbled
losing means a letter is taken away before the jumbling
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Chaotic Conservatives, gutted every day, lose their sense of togetherness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of their' is E; 'losing' removes it from TORIESDAILY and 'Disarrayed' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity and mutual support within a group, a shared common purpose.

clue.text: Loving the quantity of activity?

parts.note: ado is fuss or bustle
a ration is a fixed amount or quantity

explanation.surface: A question on how much affection fits into all the busy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the quantity of activity' read backwards in order gives ADO then RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship, a noun matching the gerund loving.

clue.text: I note disease from here having no initial effect

parts.note: flu is a common illness

indicators.note: drops the first letter of the word for from here

parts.note: hence means from this place

explanation.surface: Someone notes that an illness spreading from here has no immediate impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no initial' takes H off HENCE, leaving ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence is the power to affect, so it means effect as a noun.

clue.text: Instrument seen in small group, nothing more

parts.note: a cell is a small unit of an organisation
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A musician's piece is played in a small ensemble, and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large bowed string instrument.

clue.text: Medal enshrining one's departing

indicators.note: enshrining means enclosing as in a shrine, so the medal holds the numeral

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A decoration honours someone who is leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Going is leaving, departing.

clue.text: Journalist — an historic

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Journalist — an historic' with no further words; the second definition is cut short and no source gives the rest

clue.text: Foremost in pop music land it, possibly

definitions.text: Foremost in pop music land it, possibly

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first
possibly signals that these letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A top pop act might win this award by leading the music scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles MUSICLANDIT into LATINUMDISC after the P from 'Foremost in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An award for huge record sales, achieved by acts at the top of the pop charts.

clue.text: Golf club not against hair accessory

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for against is removed

parts.note: a driver is a golf club used off the tee
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A golf club declares it is not opposed to a hair device.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdryer is an appliance for hair, also spelt this way.

clue.text: Island language in modern times?

definitions.meaning: a computer programming language, a modern sort of language

explanation.surface: An island whose tongue has changed in recent years.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an Indonesian island and a widely used computer programming language.

clue.text: What sounds like top dog

indicators.note: what sounds like signals a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a peak is a top or summit

explanation.surface: A question on what resembles the leading dog.
explanation.walkthrough: PEKE is a short name for the Pekingese, a small dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Pekingese, a small long-haired breed.

clue.text: Flower from Dublin, cut

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something from Dublin is Irish

explanation.surface: A blossom from Ireland's capital, trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the final H off IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a plant with showy blooms.

clue.text: Get rid of girl I detest, retaining one hint of love

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the word for detest encloses the letters

parts.note: to hate is to detest
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone wants to be rid of a girl they loathe while keeping a little love.
explanation.definitionFit: To annihilate is to destroy or wipe out entirely.

clue.text: What bring point to every Christmas, ultimately?

definitions.text: What bring point to every Christmas, ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of each of these words in turn

explanation.surface: A question about what gives the festive season its purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of 'point to every Christmas'; the whole clue then describes presents for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Playthings for children are what make the festive season worthwhile.

clue.text: Soldiers to regard reorganising as not progressive

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps

indicators.note: reorganising means putting in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops view a shake-up as a step backward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganising' turns TOREGARD into TROGRADE, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde means moving backwards or reverting, the opposite of advancing.
